ownerCommand.copy: Bring branch operations, cash exposure, stock issues, approvals, reconciliation breaks, payroll readiness, and close status into view.
ownerCommand.proof: Operational signals lead back to the workflow and evidence that produced them.

accountantCollaboration.label: accountant collaboration
accountantCollaboration.title: Review the books without reconstructing operations
accountantCollaboration.copy: Give accounting teams source-linked journals, reconciliation status, supporting evidence, review queues, and close packs.
accountantCollaboration.proof: Operational documents, ledger entries, reviewer notes, and exported evidence can share a traceable path.

accessApprovals.label: roles and approvals
accessApprovals.title: Separate action, approval, and release
accessApprovals.copy: Apply role boundaries and maker-checker review to sensitive stock, payment, payroll, accounting, and compliance work.
accessApprovals.proof: Permission scope, approval state, actor identity, and decision history stay explicit.

groupOversight.label: group oversight
groupOversight.title: Govern several entities without flattening their context
groupOversight.copy: Compare organizations, branches, modules, exceptions, and close readiness while preserving each operating boundary.
groupOversight.proof: Tenant, entity, branch, role, and module scope remain part of every review.

pricing.title: Build the operating system your business needs now, with room to extend.
pricing.description: Every rollout starts with a shared platform foundation, then combines operating paths and controlled extensions around the work, evidence, and support your team actually needs.

foundation.label: always included
foundation.title: Platform Foundation
foundation.copy: The tenant shell and core controls stay consistent across every path. They are the operating foundation, not a module sold back to the customer.

points.scope: Organization, location, user, and permission scope
points.evidence: Baseline security, audit, and operating evidence controls

paths.label: three connected paths
paths.intro: Start with one coherent business outcome. Paths can be combined, but required dependencies and release readiness are confirmed before scope is committed.

operations.name: Operations Core
operations.outcome: Create one dependable operating record across stock, buying, selling, suppliers, customers, locations, and daily reporting.
operations.bestFor: Retailers, distributors, and stock-led teams replacing disconnected operational tools

points.a: Inventory, movements, counts, transfers, and valuation context
points.b: Sales, customers, purchasing, suppliers, and approval handoffs

operations.dependency: Platform Foundation is included; retail POS and continuity are optional extensions.

finance.name: Finance and Assurance
finance.outcome: Carry operational events into finance, OHADA accounting, reconciliation, compliance review, and an explainable period close.
finance.bestFor: Growing or multi-branch businesses formalizing cash, ledger, provider, and close control

points.a: Cash visibility, receivables, payables, and finance control
points.b: OHADA accounting records with source-linked posting evidence
points.c: Reconciliation, close assurance, and qualified compliance workflows

finance.dependency: Finance and accounting establish the base; reconciliation and close layer on proven source data.
finance.commercial: Organization, assurance scope, and active provider connections

people.name: People and Payroll
people.outcome: Keep approved people facts, time, payroll inputs, outputs, payments, declarations, and ledger handoffs controlled but connected.
people.bestFor: SMBs formalizing workforce records, attendance, payroll execution, and payroll evidence

points.a: HRIS people records, organization scope, contracts, and approved changes
points.b: Presence, payroll readiness, runs, payslips, and declarations
points.c: Payment, accounting, privacy, and review evidence

people.dependency: Country, privacy, payroll, provider, and accounting readiness are confirmed before rollout.
people.commercial: Organization and active employees in a payroll period

extensions.label: dependency-aware extensions
extensions.intro: Extensions deepen a proven path. They do not silently grant source modules, skip required controls, or turn internal capabilities into disconnected products.

retail.name: Retail POS and Continuity
retail.copy: Add cashier sessions, tenders, receipts, drawers, refunds, devices, and controlled offline replay for permanent selling locations.
retail.requires: Operations Core, sales, inventory, and approved device controls
retail.driver: Active locations or terminals; hardware and payment fees remain separate

reconciliation.name: Provider Reconciliation
reconciliation.copy: Ingest provider evidence, match recorded payments, isolate suspense, route exceptions, and retain sign-off proof.
reconciliation.requires: Finance, OHADA accounting, and a validated provider adapter
reconciliation.driver: Active provider connections and qualified setup scope

production.name: Production Operations
production.copy: Connect recipes, raw materials, batches, planning, costing, yield, and profitability to inventory evidence.

intelligence.name: Intelligence and Growth
intelligence.copy: Add source-aware analytics and commercial-agent workflows without exposing data from paths the organization does not hold.
intelligence.requires: Active source paths and explicit report-access controls
intelligence.driver: Organization scope and approved source domains

delivery.label: commercial model and delivery
delivery.intro: Use charging units that follow customer value and real delivery cost. Configuration, migration, country, provider, and assurance work remain visible instead of being hidden in a misleading plan price.
delivery.modelTitle: Quote-led while regional economics and automation are validated
delivery.modelCopy: No public numeric price is presented until package composition, taxes, currency, provider costs, support obligations, and entitlement operations are approved. The units below are working hypotheses for customer discovery.

platform.name: Platform and operations
platform.basis: Organization base plus active operating locations

retail.name: Retail and devices
retail.basis: Active locations or terminals, with hardware and payment costs separated

people.name: People and payroll
people.basis: Organization base plus employees active in a payroll period

regulated.name: Assurance and adapters
regulated.basis: Provider, country, and qualified control scope

delivery.servicesTitle: Delivery services scoped to the rollout

onboarding.name: Onboarding and migration
onboarding.copy: Data mapping, opening balances, workflow setup, control validation, training, and acceptance evidence.

country.name: Country-pack setup
country.copy: Qualified rule scope, statutory configuration, provenance, limitations, and change ownership.

providers.name: Provider adapters
providers.copy: Validated integration, credential setup, event mapping, reconciliation, outage handling, and support boundaries.

assurance.name: Assurance and support
assurance.copy: Close onboarding, review routines, response targets, operational guidance, and managed support where contracted.

cta.label: qualified rollout request
cta.title: Plan the smallest coherent rollout, then expand on evidence.
cta.copy: Choose the first operating outcome, confirm dependencies and data readiness, and add extensions only when they create measurable control or capacity.
cta.note: Availability is confirmed against country, provider, security, migration, and release readiness. This is not instant self-service activation.

finalCta.title: Bring daily operations into one explainable OHADA record.
finalCta.copy: Start with POS, inventory, purchasing, and payments. Expand into reconciliation, OHADA accounting, compliance, payroll, and close assurance as the evidence trail matures.

footer.subtitle: OHADA operating system
footer.copy: A ledger-first operating layer for OHADA businesses that need POS, stock, purchasing, payments, finance, compliance, payroll, reconciliation, and branch controls to speak the same truth.
footer.copyright: Stoquify. Built for disciplined OHADA operations.

peopleToPay.title: Keep people truth separate from payroll execution, but never disconnected.
peopleToPay.description: Stoquify already contains a permission-gated HRIS foundation. The operating model makes its responsibility explicit: HRIS owns approved people facts; payroll consumes approved inputs; payments, declarations, and accounting retain their own proof.

people.title: HRIS people truth
people.copy: People identity, organization scope, contracts, compensation, time, leave, approvals, self-service, and movement history.

payroll.title: Payroll readiness
payroll.copy: Approved people facts become controlled payroll inputs without allowing payroll to overwrite HRIS truth.

proof.title: Payments and declarations
proof.copy: Payslips, payment evidence, statutory declarations, provider state, and exceptions remain distinct.

close.title: Accounting and close
close.copy: Payroll postings, liabilities, reconciliation, corrections, and close assurance connect back to source.

peopleToPay.statusTitle: The HRIS core is present behind role controls
peopleToPay.statusBody: The repository includes people directories and profiles, manager and employee self-service, approvals, movement history, contracts, compensation, time and leave, document evidence, organization scope, and payroll-readiness services.
peopleToPay.boundaryBody: The latest readiness evidence approves a controlled local pilot, not an unrestricted production claim. Final environment, provider, authority, deployment, and release evidence must still be proven.
